lent-17.quote: So then by our faith in Him He has made our love to God and our neighbour to grow, making us godly and righteous and good.
lent-17.who: St. Irenaeus, Demonstration of the Apostolic Preaching
lent-17.question: Which small, concrete act of love toward God or neighbor will you do this week to let your love grow, rather than merely hoping it will?

lent-18.quote: For whosoever superintends the healing of wounds must needs administer in wine the smart of pain, and in oil the softness of loving-kindness, to the end that through wine what is festering may be purged, and through oil what is curable may be soothed.
lent-18.who: St. Gregory the Great, Pastoral Rule
lent-18.question: Whose wound near you needs both firmness and gentleness from you today, and what is one way you can tend it rather than walk past?

lent-19.quote: God is all this to thee: if thou hungerest, He is bread to thee; if thou thirstest, He is water to thee; if thou art in darkness, He is light to thee: for He remains incorruptible.
lent-19.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-19.question: Where in your life are you walking in darkness, and what would it mean today to let Christ be the light you walk by?

lent-20.quote: But because “the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us,” by His very nativity he made an eye-salve to cleanse the eyes of our heart, and to enable us to see His majesty by means of His humility.
lent-20.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-20.question: What can you see now, through Christ's humility, that you could not see at the start of Lent, and how will you act on it?

lent-21.quote: If we thirst, let us come; and not by our feet, but by our affections; let us come, not by removing from our place, but by loving.
lent-21.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-21.question: What are you truly thirsting for today, and what would it mean to come to Christ by loving someone rather than by going anywhere?

lent-22.quote: But He who was asking drink was thirsting for the faith of the woman herself.
lent-22.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-22.question: Christ asks you for a drink of faith. What small, honest offering of trust can you give Him today?

lent-23.quote: There is, indeed, this resurrection which comes to pass now; unbelievers were dead, the unrighteous were dead; the righteous live, they pass from the death of unbelief to the life of faith.
lent-23.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-23.question: Where have you passed, or still need to pass, from unbelief to faith, and whom can you welcome back to life alongside you?

lent-24.quote: Let us remit, that we may have remission: let us grant the pardon which we crave: let us not be eager to be revenged when we pray to be forgiven.
lent-24.question: Who owes you an apology you are still waiting for, and what pardon will you grant today before you ask to be forgiven?

lent-25.quote: We pray with closed doors when with closed lips and complete silence we pray to the searcher not of words but of hearts.
lent-25.question: If God listens to the heart rather than to words, what could you leave unsaid and simply offer Him in ten silent minutes today?

lent-26.quote: Let those who wish Christ to spare them, have mercy on the poor; let them give freely to feed the wretched, who desire to attain to the society of the blessed.
lent-26.question: Whom among the poor can you feed this week, and what will you give up in order to do it?

lent-27.quote: The Fast should not end with abstinence from food, but lead to good deeds.
lent-27.question: Beyond what you are giving up, what good deed will your fast become today, and for whom?

lent-28.quote: Observe how He leadeth her mind upward; for to raise Lazarus was not the only thing sought; it was necessary that both she and they who were with her should learn the Resurrection.
lent-28.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John
lent-28.question: What is one tomb in your life, a habit or a grief, where you can trust that Christ gives life now, not only on the last day?

lent-29.quote: Therefore He said not, “Let him renounce himself unto death,” but, “Let him take up his cross;” setting forth the reproachful death; and that not once, nor twice, but throughout all life one ought so to do.
lent-29.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
lent-29.question: Where is Christ asking you to deny yourself not once but daily, and what is one concrete way you will carry that cross today?

lent-30.quote: But the height of His glorification had to be preceded by the depth of His passion.
lent-30.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-30.question: What must fall into the ground and die in you, a comfort or a grudge, so that fruit can come before Easter?

lent-31.quote: Consequently, that the cause of all diseases might be cured, namely, pride, the Son of God came down and was made low.
lent-31.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-31.question: Where does pride keep you from stepping lower this week, and what lowly act of service can you offer in imitation of Christ?

lent-32.quote: Sometimes I consider myself there, as a stone before a carver, whereof he is to make a statue: presenting myself thus before God, I desire Him to make His perfect image in my soul, and render me entirely like Himself.
lent-32.who: Brother Lawrence, The Practice of the Presence of God
lent-32.question: What in your heart would you ask God to carve away, and will you sit still before Him for five minutes to let Him begin?

lent-33.quote: Let all men’s faith then be established, according to the preaching of the most holy Gospel, and let no one be ashamed of Christ’s cross, through which the world was redeemed.
lent-33.question: Where are you tempted to be ashamed of Christ or of the cross, and how can you quietly acknowledge Him there this week?

lent-34.quote: That same Jesus Christ our Lord, that same Jesus exactly, He is the complete Physician of our wounds.
lent-34.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-34.question: Which of your wounds, hidden or obvious, have you not yet brought to the Physician who bore His own for you? Bring one today.

lent-35.quote: And the cause of our restoration is naught else but the mercy of God, Whom we should not have loved, unless He had first loved us, and dispelled the darkness of our ignorance by the light of His truth.
lent-35.question: Whose love first reached you before you deserved it, and how can you love someone first today, without waiting to be loved?

lent-36.quote: What moves You to do us such mercy through pure love, and on account of no debt that You owed us, or need that You had of us?
lent-36.who: St. Catherine of Siena, The Dialogue
lent-36.question: God owed you nothing, yet gave everything. To whom can you show unearned kindness today, someone you owe nothing at all?

lent-37.quote: I seek the bread of God, which is the flesh of Jesus Christ; and I seek His blood, a drink which is love incorruptible.
lent-37.who: St. Ignatius of Antioch, Letter to the Romans
lent-37.question: What hunger in you has been feeding on lesser things, and how will you let Christ be the bread you truly seek today?

lent-38.quote: This is the reason for the sojourn of Christ in the flesh, the pattern life described in the Gospels, the sufferings, the cross, the tomb, the resurrection; so that the man who is being saved through imitation of Christ receives that old adoption.
lent-38.who: St. Basil the Great, On the Holy Spirit
lent-38.question: Which step of Christ's way, from His sufferings to the cross and the tomb, are you being asked to imitate this week, and how?

lent-39.quote: For that which was and is a reproach to Him, and for His sake to us, even the cross, this same is, says he, His government, being a sign of His kingdom.
lent-39.who: St. Irenaeus, Demonstration of the Apostolic Preaching
lent-39.question: The cross, once a reproach, is Christ's sign of kingship. What reproach or humiliation might you accept today as a way of following your King?

lent-40.quote: The branches of palm trees are laudatory emblems, significant of victory, because the Lord was about to overcome death by dying, and by the trophy of His cross to triumph over the devil, the prince of death.
lent-40.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-40.question: The crowd waved palms for a King who would conquer by dying. How will you welcome Him this week, even when it costs you?

lent-41.quote: Helpless, I cast myself at the feet of Jesus, I watered them with my tears, I wiped them with my hair: and then I subdued my rebellious body with weeks of abstinence.
lent-41.question: Mary poured out something precious at Jesus' feet. What precious thing, time, money, or pride, will you pour out for Him today?

lent-42.quote: The Lord Jesus declares that He is giving His disciples a new commandment, that they should love one another.
lent-42.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John
lent-42.question: Which person is hardest for you to love as Christ has loved you, and what is one concrete act of love toward them today?

lent-43.quote: Return to thy right mind; lay aside thy madness and be wise. Mercy invites thee, Salvation knocks at the door, Life recalls thee to life.
lent-43.question: Christ keeps calling even the one about to betray Him. Where are you resisting His patient mercy, and what would returning to your right mind look like?

lent-44.quote: Judge not the matter from the taste, but from faith be fully assured without misgiving, that the Body and Blood of Christ have been vouchsafed to thee.
lent-44.who: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Mystagogic Catecheses
lent-44.question: Tonight, how will you meet Christ in the Eucharist by faith rather than by feeling, and whom will you then serve as He served?

lent-45.quote: Among all the works of God’s mercy, dearly-beloved, which from the beginning have been bestowed upon men’s salvation, none is more wondrous, and none more sublime, than that Christ was crucified for the world.
lent-45.question: Christ was crucified for the world, and for you. In silence before the cross today, what do you want to say to Him?

lent-46.quote: A medicine of life has entered into Hell, and has restored life to its dead.
lent-46.who: St. Ephrem the Syrian, Nisibene Hymns
lent-46.question: Christ is at work even in the silence of the tomb. Where are you waiting today, and can you wait there in trust?
